answer: Each identity runs one walnut-oil press in a cedar barrel, locking a 68-credit bond and filing one sheet. First filing costs 28 credits; the kth costs 28+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6022 and 1000 fakes pay 3,025,000 in fees plus 68,000 locked. An auditor at the wharf depot recomputes oil yield from walnut input weight with the press table: excess oil, a reused seal, or a duplicate batch burns the bond. A rented-press ring fails because a rented sheet carries the lender's key and its batch appears elsewhere, so both bonds burn. An honest presser pays 28 once, bond returned after a clean epoch.
